objects.description: No user-defined types are defined in this header. It only declares utility functions and a macro. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to document.

functions.name: xmalloc
functions.description: Allocate a memory block of the requested size, with an internal NULL check. Intended as a safer malloc wrapper that handles allocation failure (likely by aborting or otherwise not returning NULL). Returns a pointer to the allocated block on success. Usage: call to allocate size bytes; free with free when done. Specific failure behavior is not documented here.
requirements: size should be the number of bytes to allocate; typical usage allows 0 but the behavior for size==0 is unknown
The returned pointer should be freed with free (or a compatible deallocator) when no longer needed
Behavior on allocation failure is unspecified here (commonly xmalloc exits instead of returning NULL); callers should not rely on NULL being returned
Thread-safety and alignment guarantees are as per the underlying allocator; no additional guarantees documented

functions.name: xrealloc
functions.description: Reallocate a memory block to a new size, with an internal NULL check. Intended as a safer realloc wrapper that handles allocation failure (likely by aborting or otherwise not returning NULL). If p is NULL, behaves like allocation of size bytes. Returns a pointer to the (possibly moved) block on success.
requirements: p must be either NULL or a pointer obtained from a compatible allocator (e.g., malloc/xmalloc/realloc family)
size is the new size in bytes; behavior for size==0 is unknown
On success, the old pointer p must not be used; use the returned pointer instead
The returned pointer should be freed with free (or a compatible deallocator) when no longer needed
Behavior on allocation failure is unspecified here (commonly xrealloc exits instead of returning NULL); callers should not rely on NULL being returned

functions.name: uppercase
functions.description: Convert the given C string to upper case in place. Returns s for convenience. Intended for ASCII/locale-default transformations; specifics about locale or encoding are not documented.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, writable, null-terminated C string
The buffer referenced by s must be large enough to hold the transformed string in place (no growth expected for ASCII)
Behavior on non-ASCII/locale-specific characters is unspecified

functions.name: lowercase
functions.description: Convert the given C string to lower case in place. Returns s for convenience. Intended for ASCII/locale-default transformations; specifics about locale or encoding are not documented.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, writable, null-terminated C string
The buffer referenced by s must be large enough to hold the transformed string in place (no growth expected for ASCII)
Behavior on non-ASCII/locale-specific characters is unspecified

functions.name: endswith
functions.description: Check whether the string str ends with the given suffix. Returns true if str has suffix as its final substring, otherwise false. Matching appears case-sensitive; no special handling for locales or encodings is documented.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string
suffix must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string
Empty suffix behavior is unspecified (commonly considered true)

functions.name: get_sig_name
functions.signature: int get_sig_name(int sig, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: Write a human-readable signal name for the signal number sig into buf. Returns an int status code (exact semantics not documented here). Typical usage: provide a buffer and its length; on success buf contains a null-terminated signal name such as "SIGHUP".
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL writable buffer
len must specify the size of buf in bytes and be large enough to hold the resulting string including the terminating null; required minimum size is not documented
sig should be a valid signal number for the target platform; behavior for invalid values is unspecified
Return value semantics (0/negative/length) are not documented; callers should check the return and/or resulting buffer defensively

functions.name: get_sig
functions.description: Return the signal number corresponding to a string like "SIGHUP". Returns an int code; exact error signaling for unknown names is not documented.
requirements: sig_name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string and should be of the form "SIG..." (e.g., "SIGHUP")
Behavior for unknown or malformed names is unspecified (may return -1 or 0 depending on implementation)
Case sensitivity of the input is not documented

functions.name: open_uri
functions.description: Open the given URI with the system’s default application. Returns an int status code; exact success/error conventions are not documented. Typical behavior may delegate to platform-specific mechanisms (e.g., xdg-open, open, or ShellExecute).
requirements: uri must be a non-NULL, null-terminated C string representing a valid URI or path
The URI must be acceptable to the underlying OS mechanism; unsupported schemes or invalid URIs may fail
Return value semantics are unspecified; callers should treat nonzero/negative values as potential errors depending on implementation

data_types.description: A C-style string buffer terminated by a NUL byte ('\0'). May contain arbitrary bytes except the terminating NUL at the end. Used by functions expecting const char* or char* and operating on the string content.

A string representing a POSIX signal name, typically of the form "SIG" followed by an uppercase identifier (e.g., "SIGHUP", "SIGINT", "SIGTERM"). Input may also be malformed or nonstandard; parsers may accept or reject variants depending on implementation.

generators.generator:
import random
import os
import string
from typing import List

# This generator focuses on producing interesting, valid C NUL-terminated strings
# that exercise:
# - uppercase/lowercase in-place ASCII transformations
# - endswith comparisons with various edge cases (empty suffix, full-match, partial, case differences)
# - get_sig with both valid and invalid signal names in varying cases
#
# The fuzzing harness requests strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string) which will
# be NUL-terminated by the stub. We must return a single bytes buffer that the fuzzing
# framework will split to feed those calls. Without a specified framing protocol from
# the harness, we generate a single buffer containing multiple NUL-terminated segments
# so that different calls can draw meaningful substrings from it. Each segment is a
# well-formed C string (no embedded NULs) and the overall blob remains under 4096 bytes.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a corpus of interesting strings for case conversion
# - Build suffix pairs (string and suffix) encoded as consecutive NUL-terminated strings
# - Build a corpus of signal names including valid POSIX names and variants
# - Add random-length mixed strings to increase coverage
# - Concatenate segments separated by single NUL bytes; end with an extra NUL for safety
#
# The fuzzer framework's FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically consumes arbitrary bytes up to a NUL,
# so providing many NUL-separated strings increases the chance of useful inputs.

POSIX_SIGNALS = [
    "SIGHUP", "SIGINT", "SIGQUIT", "SIGILL", "SIGTRAP", "SIGABRT", "SIGBUS", "SIGFPE",
    "SIGKILL", "SIGUSR1", "SIGSEGV", "SIGUSR2", "SIGPIPE", "SIGALRM", "SIGTERM",
    "SIGCHLD", "SIGCONT", "SIGSTOP", "SIGTSTP", "SIGTTIN", "SIGTTOU", "SIGURG",
    "SIGXCPU", "SIGXFSZ", "SIGVTALRM", "SIGPROF", "SIGWINCH", "SIGIO", "SIGPWR",
    "SIGSYS"
]

# Common URI schemes for open_uri (not used in target fuzzers but still valid strings)
URI_SAMPLES = [
    "http://example.com/",
    "https://example.com/path?x=1#frag",
    "file:///etc/hosts",
    "mailto:user@example.com",
    "ftp://ftp.example.com/pub/",
    "data:text/plain,Hello%20World",
]

CASE_STRINGS = [
    "",  # empty string
    "a", "Z", "0", "9",
    "abc", "XYZ", "AbC123",
    "hello world", "TeSt-Ing_123", "snake_case", "kebab-case", "PascalCase", "camelCase",
    "MiXeD caSe WiTh SpAcEs",
    "éàçñ",  # non-ASCII to test pass-through/unspecified behavior
    "ASCII-only!@#$%^&*()_+[]{};:'\",.<>/?\\|`~",
    "endwithsuffix", "endsWithSuffix",
]

SUFFIX_PAIRS = [
    ("hello", ""),
    ("", ""),
    ("", "nonempty"),
    ("foobar", "bar"),
    ("foobar", "baz"),
    ("CaseTest", "test"),  # case mismatch
    ("CaseTest", "Test"),
    ("aaaaa", "aaa"),
    ("short", "longsuffix"),
    ("exact", "exact"),
]

MIX_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+@[]{}()!,?%#<>|^$*~"  # no NULs


def _rand_str(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: str = MIX_CHARS) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _valid_signal_variants(sig: str) -> List[str]:
    # Generate case and prefix variants for get_sig
    base = sig
    variants = [
        base,
        base.lower(),
        base.capitalize(),
        base.replace("SIG", "sig"),
        base[3:],  # without SIG
        base[3:].lower(),
        "SIG" + base[3:].lower(),
        "SIG" + base[3:],
    ]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(variants))


def _make_sig_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Include canonical names and variants
    for s in POSIX_SIGNALS:
        out.extend(_valid_signal_variants(s))
    # Add numeric-like and malformed names
    out.extend([
        "SIG0", "SIG1", "SIG2", "SIG9", "SIG15",
        "SIG", "SIGXYZ", "SIGSEGV2", "SIGINTERRUPT",
        "HUP", "INT", "TERM",
    ])
    # Sprinkle random strings that look like signals
    for _ in range(20):
        name = "SIG" + _rand_str(rng, 1, 8, string.ascii_uppercase)
        out.append(name)
    rng.shuffle(out)
    return out


def _encode_c_str(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode to UTF-8 but ensure no embedded NULs; replace NULs if any
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    if b"\x00" in b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"?")
    return b + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Case transformation strings
    # Mix curated and random strings
    case_list = CASE_STRINGS[:]
    # Add random ASCII strings with mixed cases
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 15)):
        s = _rand_str(rng, 0, rng.randint(1, 64))
        # Inject some alternating case patterns
        if s:
            alt = ''.join(ch.upper() if i % 2 else ch.lower() for i, ch in enumerate(s))
            case_list.append(alt)
        case_list.append(s)
    # Add strings with long runs
    case_list.append("a" * 256)
    case_list.append("Z" * 256)
    case_list.append("Az" * 128)

    rng.shuffle(case_list)
    for s in case_list[:rng.randint(10, 40)]:
        parts.append(_encode_c_str(s))

    # 2) endswith pairs: encode as str\0suffix\0 to pack contiguous candidates
    # Provide many pairs, including randoms designed to match and not match
    pair_count = rng.randint(8, 24)
    pool = SUFFIX_PAIRS[:]
    for _ in range(pair_count):
        # Generate random pair sometimes matching
        base = _rand_str(rng, 0, rng.randint(0, 64))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            # choose a suffix from base
            cut = rng.randint(0, len(base))
            suf = base[cut:]
        else:
            # unrelated suffix
            suf = _rand_str(rng, 0, rng.randint(0, 32))
        pool.append((base, suf))
    rng.shuffle(pool)

    for s, suf in pool[:pair_count]:
        parts.append(_encode_c_str(s))
        parts.append(_encode_c_str(suf))

    # 3) get_sig corpus
    sigs = _make_sig_corpus(rng)
    # Also include some URIs and random strings to mix into name space
    extras = URI_SAMPLES[:]
    for _ in range(10):
        extras.append(_rand_str(rng, 1, 20))
    rng.shuffle(extras)

    sig_take = min(len(sigs), rng.randint(20, 80))
    for s in sigs[:sig_take]:
        parts.append(_encode_c_str(s))
    for s in extras[:rng.randint(3, 12)]:
        parts.append(_encode_c_str(s))

    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes
    blob = b"".join(parts)
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        # Truncate at last NUL before limit to keep final segment valid
        cut = blob.rfind(b"\x00", 0, 4096)
        if cut == -1:
            blob = blob[:4096-1] + b"\x00"
        else:
            blob = blob[:cut+1]

    # End with an extra NUL for safety
    if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
        blob += b"\x00"
    return blob
